title: Checkout: a Mermaid flow from the doc, reshaped with icons and the VPC picture from the infra repo
persona: A payments engineer who already has the checkout flow as Mermaid in a design doc and an exported VPC diagram, and wants to show where the slow, uncertain call is.
topic: why declined cards make checkout slow
realism: Nobody redraws what they already have: they paste the doc's Mermaid, drop in the infra diagram, then add the parts the doc never showed (the phone, the database, a queue, Stripe) and argue about one call.

steps.say: I already had the checkout flow as Mermaid in our design doc, so I'll start from that.

mermaid.source:
flowchart LR
  A[Checkout] --> B{Card ok?}
  B -->|yes| C[Order placed]
  B -->|no| D[Show error]

steps.say: The user is on the phone app.
When the order is placed it's written to the database, and an event goes on a queue.
The card check calls Stripe, I think synchronously, but I'm not sure.

steps.say: And this is the VPC picture from our infra repo, the card vault and the fraud scorer live in there.
The queue is new, we're adding it in this change.
This call is the slow one when the card is declined.

steps.note: is the Stripe call inside the DB transaction?

steps.say: That's the part I want explained.

story: The checkout flow (Checkout → Card ok? → Order placed / Show error) came from Mermaid they already had; they added the phone, the database, the queue and Stripe around it.
The database icon was renamed to Orders DB.
They are unsure whether the card check calls Stripe synchronously; that arrow is dashed and labeled 'sync?'.
The Payment events queue is new in this change.
The dropped VPC picture shows the Card vault and the Fraud scorer inside the Payments VPC.
The call they say is slow when a card is declined is the one from 'Card ok?' to Stripe (they pointed at both).
partner_should_ask_about: whether the Stripe call happens inside the DB transaction
what happens on the decline path before Show error
